study.title: LOPA – Propane storage and propane–air dilution system (worked example)
study.unit: Utilities – LPG (propane) storage, vaporisation and propane–air (SNG) dilution
study.team: G. Safety (LOPA facilitator), C. Process (process), E. Instrument (instrument / SIS), D. Operator (LPG plant operations), F. Mechanical (relief and mechanical)
study.hazopTitle: PHA / HAZOP – Propane storage and propane–air dilution system (worked example)
study.scope: The four HAZOP deviations ticked LOPA: bullet overfill (N01-06), loss of propane to the mixer (N03-01), tanker drive-away (N01-10) and bullet overpressure during unloading (N01-04). Illustrative values for training – not design data.

settings.basis: Typical example values – replace with the client's tolerable risk criteria before the study.

scenarios.node: N01 – Node 301 – Road tanker unloading to propane storage T-1/T-2/T-3
scenarios.deviation: Higher level in storage tank T-1/T-2/T-3 (overfill)
scenarios.cause: Transfer not stopped at high level (source)
scenarios.consequence: Source: tank pressurisation. Correctly: the bullet fills liquid-full; liquid propane reaches the relief valves – liquid relief and a large two-phase release at the tank farm; hydraulic overpressure of the liquid-full bullet as it warms

ie.desc: Transfer not stopped at high level (source)
ie.basis: About 150 deliveries a year × 1E-3 per delivery that the operator does not stop at the fill limit (checklist in use) – illustrative

modifiers.desc: Probability of delayed ignition of the propane vented by the relief valves
modifiers.basis: CCPS ECCM (2014) §3.3 default (Moosemiller 2009); the operator and the driver attend every delivery, so no presence credit

ipls.name: LT-11/21/31 – High-high level trip LAHH (85 %) from LT-11/21/31 closes ROV-11/21/31 and stops the compressors (source: LT closes ROV)
ipls.basis: FT-PR-01 gate G-005 – LAHH trip fails to close ROV-11 (PFDavg from the fault tree)

adj.evidence: FT-PR-01 G-005; SRS draft for LAHH-11/21/31; proof-test records 2026
adj.conditions: Annual proof test of LT-11/21/31 and ROV-11/21/31 kept in the plan

ipls.name: LT-11/21/31 – High level alarm LAH at 80 % with operator response (stop unloading)
ipls.basis: FT-PR-01 gate G-004 – LAH not acted on

adj.evidence: FT-PR-01: LAH and LAHH share LT-11/21/31; the fault tree gives 3.9E-3 for both together, not 0.109 × 0.0112 = 1.2E-3
adj.reason: Not independent of the LAHH trip – both take their signal from LT-11/21/31

ipls.name: Independent high-high level switch LSHH-11/21/31 on its own tapping, SIL 2, closing ROV-11/21/31 (recommendation)
ipls.basis: Proposed – SIL 2 assumed; illustrative

others: Tanker unloading procedure OP-PR-010 and checklist: ullage check before unloading, operator in attendance throughout
PSV-11/21/31 – Bullet relief valves PSV-11/21/31 at 17.5 barg, fire-case sized, discharging vertically upwards (source: 'PSV provided')
scenarios.notes: FT-PR-01 gives an overfill frequency of 1.9E-3 /yr with both protections. The LOPA rejects the LAH credit because it shares the transmitter with the trip – the same dependency the fault tree models.

alarp.options: Second level measurement, reduced fill limit, automatic stop of the unloading compressor
alarp.decision: Further risk reduction is reasonably practicable – recommendation raised
alarp.justification: The gap is closed only by an independent level switch – recommendation raised

scenarios.result: SIL 2 needed (Safety, RRF 505); with proposed IPLs: Gap ≤ 10× – one more IPL or SIL 1 – accepted IPLs only

scenarios.node: N03 – Node 303 – Propane dilution system (propane–air mixing station)
scenarios.deviation: Less / no propane to the mixer while air continues – mixture moves into the flammable range
scenarios.cause: Loss of propane vapour supply (vaporiser trip, PCV-01 closes, header low pressure)
scenarios.consequence: Propane fraction falls from 55 % towards the flammable range (below 9.5 % in air) – explosive mixture in the mixer, surge tank ST-01 and the header to the burners; ignition at a burner flashes back – internal explosion of ST-01 and the header

ie.desc: Loss of propane vapour supply (vaporiser trip, PCV-01 closes, header low pressure)
ie.basis: FT-PR-02 event BE-001: loss of propane vapour supply – 0.5 /yr

modifiers.desc: Probability that a person is present at the mixing station
modifiers.basis: Unattended station; rounds about 17 h a week – CCPS ECCM (2014) Table 3.4

ipls.basis: FT-PR-02 gate G-003 – PSLL-01 fails to stop the air

ipls.name: AT-01 – Calorimeter / Wobbe analyser AT-01 with low-heating-value trip (independent of FFIC-01)
ipls.basis: FT-PR-02 gate G-004 – calorimeter trip AT-01 fails

adj.conditions: Monthly calibration check of AT-01 kept in the plan

ipls.name: Propane / air ratio trip on an independent propane flow meter, SIL 2 (recommendation)
ipls.basis: Proposed – SIL 2 assumed; illustrative

others: FFIC-01 – Propane / air ratio controller FFIC-01 with cross-limiting (air follows propane)
FA-01 – In-line flame arrester FA-01 on the propane–air header to the users
scenarios.notes: FT-PR-02 quantifies the same protection: PSLL-01 and AT-01 together fail with PFD 1.8E-2.

alarp.options: Independent ratio trip; nitrogen blanketing of the surge tank
alarp.decision: Further risk reduction is reasonably practicable – recommendation raised
alarp.justification: Recommendation raised for the ratio trip

scenarios.result: SIL 2 needed (Safety, RRF 875); with proposed IPLs: Gap ≤ 10× – one more IPL or SIL 1 – accepted IPLs only

ipls.name: Unloading compressor trip on high bullet pressure, independent of the pressure gauges, SIL 1 (recommendation)
ipls.basis: Proposed – SIL 1 assumed; illustrative
